exercise.name: Single Arm Dumbbell Curl over Incline Bench
aliases: One-arm curl over an incline bench

reference.title: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Curl (over incline bench)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, Bench, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.5 s squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight. Lower under control into the straight-arm position; do not bounce off the pad at the bottom (clinical opinion).

cues.text: Set the back pad steep (about 65 degrees). Stand behind it, lean in so the right armpit rests on the top edge and lay the back of the right upper arm along the pad, palm up; left hand on the top of the pad.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward the shoulder; the upper arm stays on the pad.
Squeeze at the top for a moment.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the arm is almost straight along the pad.
Short pause near straight, repeat; then switch arms.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the elbow off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the back of the upper arm pressed into the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping into a fully locked, bouncing bottom
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and stop just short of locking out.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the shoulder over the pad to lift
mistakes.fix: Keep the armpit on the top edge and the trunk still.

mistakes.mistake: Wrist curling to finish the rep
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: Preacher-style curls use a shorter range than the standing curl: about 116 degrees versus 132 degrees for the dumbbell curl (Oliveira 2009)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Upper arm fixed on the pad, flexed forward of the trunk; biceps activity peaked near 75 degrees of shoulder flexion in an isometric curl (Moon 2013)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)
Steep back pad so the armpit rests on the top edge while standing (common practice, clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm on the pad (mesh gap)
kinematics.norm: The back of the upper arm stays on the pad the whole rep (clinical opinion)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Elbow strain at the bottom: do not let the dumbbell drop or bounce into a locked elbow (clinical opinion).
modify: Elbow discomfort at the bottom: stop a little short of straight.
Armpit pressure: put a folded towel on the pad edge.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor; with the back of the arm on the pad (preacher style) the load is highest early in the lift, near straight arms. Preacher-style curls grew the distal biceps (Zabaleta-Korta 2023), and training the initial (lengthened) range of the curl gave larger gains at the distal biceps than the final range (Pedrosa 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still against the pad.

guides.label: Dumbbell curls up off the pad
